- If sentiment is consistently low (≤0.25) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 1.5x prior high or adjust downward by 2–5% after spike.
- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and model forecasts are rising, check for mean reversion; if price has been rising >10% over 5d, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to avoid overbought bias.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–3 days (especially in 30d horizon), model may be overreacting to sentiment; adjust forecast downward by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment (e.g., 0.0–0.3) and model forecasts are high, apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid sentiment mismatch.
- For 30d forecasts, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% over 3–5 consecutive days, apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overfitting to recent momentum.
